methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring

methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.9x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Signaloid is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $10M to date. The valuation universe for frontier chip design includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage peers across the Chips & Semiconductors sector, though a tightly filtered peer set at Signaloid's specific stage and tier proved insufficient for reliable median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method here. Using $10M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $25M. Public Semiconductors trade at a 18.9x median P/S multiple, but this cannot be applied without Signaloid's revenue, which is not disclosed. Peer-median triangulation failed to converge: the broader Chips & Semiconductors universe includes 13 companies, but adjacent-stage filtering and valuation-tier matching did not produce the three or more datapoints required for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, centered on $25M. This estimate rests on a single methodology and therefore carries material uncertainty. Key risks include the early-stage nature of the company (pre-revenue or minimal revenue likely), absence of narrow peer comparables at seed funding stage, and inability to anchor to public market multiples without disclosed revenue. Any revised valuation would benefit from additional private-market transaction data in frontier semiconductors.
